# RapiDoc Portal

> Turn OpenAPI specs and Markdown guides into a developer portal. Docs as code, static output, optional single sign-on (SSO). Part of the RapiDoc family of open-source (MIT) tools for OpenAPI and Arazzo, each with its own llms.txt: RapiDoc, the <rapi-doc> web component for interactive API references with Try, an in-browser mock and MCP server export (https://rapidocui.com/llms.txt); RapiDoc Portal, a docs-as-code developer portal built from OpenAPI specs and Markdown guides, with single sign-on and access rules (https://portal.rapidocui.com/llms.txt); RapiMock, a stateful mock server with request validation and token checks (https://mock.rapidocui.com/llms.txt); RapiFlow, the <rapi-flow> web component that draws Arazzo workflows and runs them in the browser (https://flow.rapidocui.com/llms.txt); plus RapiDoc Mini, RapiPdf (OpenAPI to PDF), the RapiDoc CLI (lint, validate, bundle, mock, MCP) and RapiDoc for Express, Fastify, Hono, FastAPI, Starlight, VitePress, Docusaurus and ASP.NET Core. How RapiDoc, RapiDoc Portal and RapiMock compare with Redocly, Scalar, Swagger, Mintlify, ReadMe, Zudoku, Docusaurus, Prism, WireMock, Mockoon, Postman and Microcks, feature by feature: https://rapidocui.com/docs/compare.md

## RapiDoc Portal

- [RapiDoc Portal documentation](https://portal.rapidocui.com/index.md): How to build a developer portal from OpenAPI specs and Markdown guides with RapiDoc Portal - configuration, guides, API reference pages, single sign-on (SSO), tools and deployment.

## Documentation

- [Introduction](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/getting-started/introduction.md): What RapiDoc Portal is, what it builds, and which package does what.
- [What's new in 1.0](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/getting-started/whats-new.md): RapiDoc Portal 1.0, in sync with RapiDoc 15 and the rest of the family. What the version promise covers, how to upgrade from 0.x, and the new sidebar.
- [Upgrading from 0.2 to 1.0](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/getting-started/upgrading-to-1-0.md): Every change to make when moving a RapiDoc Portal from 0.2 to 1.0, with the old and the new form side by side.
- [Quickstart](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): Create a portal, see it running, add your own OpenAPI spec, and build it for production.
- [Project structure](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/getting-started/project-structure.md): Where the config, specs, guides and static files go, and how files become URLs.
- [CLI](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/reference/cli.md): Every rapidoc command and option.
- [Configuration keys](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/reference/config.md): Every key of rapidoc.config.yaml in one place.
- [Programmatic API](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/reference/programmatic-api.md): Build, serve and mock portals from your own Node.js scripts.
- [How a build works](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/reference/how-it-works.md): What rapidoc dev and rapidoc build do, step by step.
- [Configuration overview](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/overview.md): How rapidoc.config.yaml is organized, its conventions, and editor autocomplete.
- [Customizing the portal](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/customizing.md): Every way to change how the portal looks and behaves - brand, layout, your own CSS, components in guides, API reference options and build scripts.
- [Site](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/site.md): Title, description, URL, logo, favicon, link previews, page titles, head tags and the announcement banner.
- [Theme](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/theme.md): Accent color, light and dark mode, and fonts.
- [Header](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/header.md): The header - links, buttons, dropdowns, mega-menus, where the tabs go and the theme switcher.
- [Navigation](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/navigation.md): Header tabs and the sidebar of each documentation tab.
- [APIs](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/apis.md): Add OpenAPI specs to the portal - ids, titles, categories, versions and remote specs.
- [Workflows](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/workflows.md): Add Arazzo specs to the portal - drawn as diagrams in your docs, runnable from the browser, and exported as MCP tools.
- [Footer](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/footer.md): Call to action, link columns, newsletter sign-up, social links and copyright.
- [Docs, search and redirects](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/docs-search-redirects.md): The docs folder, table of contents, edit links, site search and redirects.
- [LLM output](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/configuration/llms.md): Every guide as Markdown, /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt for AI tools, and Copy page buttons.
- [Markdown](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/markdown.md): Write guides in plain Markdown - titles, frontmatter, links, images and code.
- [Markdoc](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/markdoc.md): Markdoc tags for callouts, tabs, steps, cards, badges and live API operations.
- [MDX](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/mdx.md): Use components in guides with MDX - no imports needed for the portal components.
- [Callouts](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/callouts.md): Notes, tips and warnings - one look whether you write them in Markdown, MDX or Markdoc.
- [Embedding operations](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/embedding-operations.md): Put a live, interactive API operation inside a guide.
- [Your own pages](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/writing/pages.md): Add pages the portal has no page type for - a landing page, a pricing page, a full-screen demo - as Astro files in a pages/ folder.
- [Reference pages](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/api-reference/reference-pages.md): What each API's reference page shows, its URLs, and how to link to an operation.
- [API versions](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/api-reference/versions.md): Publish several versions of one API, each with its own URLs, and a version picker on the reference page.
- [API catalog](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/api-reference/catalog.md): The /catalog page - every API, grouped by category.
- [RapiDoc attributes](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/api-reference/rapidoc-attributes.md): Change how API reference pages render with the rapidoc key.
- [Single sign-on (SSO)](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/overview.md): Put the portal behind your company's single sign-on (SSO) with OpenID Connect (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google, Keycloak, Auth0), and decide who may read which pages and APIs.
- [Set up sign-in](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/setup.md): Step by step, for any OpenID Connect provider - register the portal, configure sign-in and access rules, test locally, and deploy.
- [SSO with Microsoft Entra ID](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/entra-id.md): Step by step - put the portal behind Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) single sign-on, and give groups of employees access to their APIs with app roles.
- [Identity providers](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/providers.md): The issuer URL, groups and Try audience for Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Auth0, Keycloak, Google, AWS Cognito, Ping, Authentik and Zitadel, and SAML-only providers.
- [Access rules](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/access-rules.md): Decide who may read which pages, APIs and files - by sign-in, group or email.
- [Try with the reader's token](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/try-it.md): Let Try call your API with the signed-in reader's access token.
- [Mock server](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/mock-server.md): Serve your specs with examples and generated data, validate requests, and check real OAuth scopes.
- [MCP server for agents](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/mcp-server.md): Every portal build carries its APIs and workflows as MCP tools; rapidoc serve hosts them at /mcp for AI agents, with the reader's own access.
- [Validate, lint and bundle](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/spec-checks.md): Check your portal's OpenAPI specs and Arazzo specs, lint what they need for good API pages, and bundle a spec split over several files, locally and in CI.
- [Migrating](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/migrate.md): Move a Zudoku or Redocly portal to RapiDoc Portal.
- [Static hosting](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/deploy/static-hosting.md): Deploy the built portal to GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages or any web server.
- [Deploy with rapidoc serve](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve.md): Run a portal with sign-in and access rules on Node or in Docker.
- [Render, DigitalOcean, Railway](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/deploy/cloud-platforms.md): Deploy a portal to Render, DigitalOcean App Platform or Railway, in one click from the starter or from your own repository.

## APIs

- [Bookstore API (OpenAPI)](https://portal.rapidocui.com/specs/bookstore.yaml): A small example API that shows what an API reference page looks like in RapiDoc Portal. Run npm run mock in this repository and Try calls the mock server on your machine.
